20. Case study: celecoxib versus diclofenac

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-20-case-gibleed.Rmd
book-20-case-gibleed.Rmd

What you will learn

Find the study concepts, define mutually exclusive new-user entry, account for censoring, and fit a pooled adjusted constant-hazard survival model.

You need: the Opal login from Getting started, concept discovery, and the preceding tutorial chapters. This chapter uses the two GiBleed sites. All observations are public synthetic teaching data; the numerical results are not clinical evidence.

Research question

Among people beginning celecoxib or diclofenac after a year without either drug, how does first GI bleeding during the following year differ? We adjust for age. This is a methods exercise; age adjustment alone does not identify a causal drug effect.

library(dsOMOPClient)
two_conns <- ds.omop.login(rep("https://localhost:8443", 2), user = "administrator",
  password = "password",
  server = c("north", "south"),
  resource = c(north = "omop.gibleed_north", south = "omop.gibleed_south"))$conns

The two GiBleed resources hold disjoint halves of the public GiBleed people, so no person is counted twice when the sites are pooled.

Find the drugs and outcome 

ce <- ds.omop.concept.search("celecoxib", domain = "Drug", conns = two_conns)$pooled
di <- ds.omop.concept.search("diclofenac", domain = "Drug", conns = two_conns)$pooled
gi <- ds.omop.concept.search("Gastrointestinal hemorrhage", domain = "Condition", conns = two_conns)$pooled
rbind(ce, di, gi)[c("concept_id", "concept_name", "standard_concept", "concept_class_id")]
concept_id concept_name standard_concept concept_class_id
1118088 celecoxib 200 MG Oral Capsule [Celebrex] S Branded Drug
1118084 celecoxib S Ingredient
40162359 Diclofenac Sodium 75 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet S Clinical Drug
1124300 Diclofenac S Ingredient
192671 Gastrointestinal hemorrhage S Clinical Finding 
ceid <- ce$concept_id[trimws(ce$concept_name) == "celecoxib"]
diid <- di$concept_id[trimws(di$concept_name) == "Diclofenac"]
giid <- gi$concept_id[trimws(gi$concept_name) == "Gastrointestinal hemorrhage"]

Select 1118084 (celecoxib), 1124300 (Diclofenac) and 192671 (Gastrointestinal hemorrhage), then inspect descendants. These GiBleed study-drug records are already ingredient-coded. The descendant request includes the seed by default: the celecoxib row below is self-inclusion, not a more specific product. Ingredient-to-product membership uses the ancestry hierarchy; Maps to serves a different purpose. This reduced vocabulary lacks the ingredient-to-product ancestor edge from 1118084 to 1118088. A catalogue match for the capsule therefore does not establish a descendant relationship, which is why only the seed appears below.

ce_children <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(ceid, conns = two_conns)$pooled
ce_children[c("concept_id", "concept_name")]
concept_id concept_name
1118084 celecoxib 
ds.omop.concept.locate(c(ceid, diid, giid), scope = "pooled",
  conns = two_conns)$pooled
concept_id table_name concept_column n_records n_persons
192671 condition_era condition_concept_id 475 475
192671 condition_occurrence condition_concept_id 475 475
1118084 drug_exposure drug_concept_id 1840 1840
1118084 drug_era drug_concept_id 1840 1840
1124300 drug_exposure drug_concept_id 850 850
1124300 drug_era drug_concept_id 850 850 
study_sets <- list(celecoxib = omop_concept_set(ceid, descendants = TRUE),
  diclofenac = omop_concept_set(diid, descendants = TRUE),
  bleeding = omop_concept_set(giid, descendants = TRUE))

The locator shows recorded use of both ingredient IDs and the bleeding concept. Counts are bands of five; the analysis below supplies its own exact denominators.

Define entry and washout

Choose first eligible exposure to either study drug. Require 365 observed days and no exposure to either during the preceding year. Exclude simultaneous starts so each person’s baseline treatment is unambiguous. Later switching does not change baseline treatment: this is an initial-treatment follow-up definition. Exclude any bleeding before or at entry so the outcome is first recorded bleeding after entry, rather than recurrence of a known prior outcome.

ce_event <- omop_event("drug_exposure", study_sets$celecoxib, name = "celecoxib")
di_event <- omop_event("drug_exposure", study_sets$diclofenac, name = "diclofenac")
bleed <- omop_event("condition_occurrence", study_sets$bleeding)
users <- omop_population("users", index = omop_index(omop_any_of(ce_event, di_event),
  select = "first_eligible"), filters = list(omop_observed(before = 365),
  omop_has_not(ce_event, window = omop_window(-365, -1)),
  omop_has_not(di_event, window = omop_window(-365, -1)),
  omop_has_not(bleed, window = omop_window(NULL, 0)),
  omop_not(omop_all(omop_has(ce_event, window = omop_window(0, 0)),
    omop_has(di_event, window = omop_window(0, 0))))))

Join baseline variables to censored follow-up

One row represents one person’s first eligible episode. Only the joined analysis frame is published; its dependencies remain private intermediates.

comparison <- omop_recipe(populations = list(users),
  variables = list(birth_year = omop_variable(name = "birth_year", table = "person", column = "year_of_birth"),
    birth_month = omop_variable(name = "birth_month", table = "person", column = "month_of_birth"),
    birth_day = omop_variable(name = "birth_day", table = "person", column = "day_of_birth"),
    entry = omop_date_parts("index", c("year", "month", "day"),
      date_spec = omop_date_spec(representation = "number")),
    celecoxib = omop_variable(event = ce_event,
    reducer = omop_reduce("binary", window = omop_window(0, 0)))),
  outputs = list(omop_output("baseline", rows = "users", format = "wide"),
    omop_output("survival", rows = "users", format = "survival", options = list(
      outcomes = list(bleed = bleed), tar = omop_window(1, 365),
      censor = list("observation_end", "death"))),
    omop_output("analysis", rows = "users", format = "joined", options = list(
      from = list(list(output = "baseline"), list(output = "survival")),
      how = "inner", cardinality = "one_to_one"))), publish = "analysis")
recipe_execute(comparison, out = c(analysis = "D_comparison"), conns = two_conns)

The censor list and 365-day window define the estimand. Event = 0 means censored within that follow-up, not “never bleeds”. Person rows remain private at each site.

Completed age subtracts one from the difference in calendar years when entry occurs before the birthday. We calculate it explicitly from the birth components and index-date parts below; missing birth components preserve missing age. GiBleed stores its birth components as numeric rather than integer columns, which the native age constructor does not accept. Use omop_age_at("index") where the source schema supports it; here the integral component values permit the completed-age calculation below.

Describe the arms before modelling

Follow-up starts on day 1 and ends at bleeding, death, observation end or day 365, whichever comes first. The survival output measures elapsed days as exit minus entry. A day-1 outcome would therefore have zero time; check this before taking a logarithm rather than silently adding time or dropping those events.

ds.omop.mutate("D_comparison", years = follow_up_days / 365.25,
  zero_time = ifelse(follow_up_days <= 0, 1L, 0L),
  month_difference = entry_month - birth_month, day_difference = entry_day - birth_day,
  age = entry_year - birth_year - ifelse(month_difference < 0 |
    (month_difference == 0 & day_difference < 0), 1L, 0L),
  newobj = "D_comparison_model", conns = two_conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_comparison_model$zero_time",
  datasources = two_conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_comparison_model$zero_time
#>    0   NA
#> 2630    0
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_comparison$celecoxib",
  "D_comparison$event", datasources = two_conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
0 1 NA
0 706 124 0
1 1445 355 0
NA 0 0 0

All 2,630 episodes have positive time. Treatment 0 is diclofenac and 1 is celecoxib; event 1 is bleeding and 0 is censoring. The event counts are 124 and 355 respectively. No prior bleeding is present in these synthetic data, so the exclusion leaves these counts unchanged while making the study definition explicit.

arm_summary <- do.call(rbind, lapply(0:1, function(arm) {
  ds.omop.filter("D_comparison_model", var = "celecoxib", op = "==", value = arm,
    newobj = paste0("D_arm", arm), conns = two_conns)
  aggregate <- function(column) dsBaseClient::ds.mean(paste0("D_arm", arm, "$", column),
    type = "combine", datasources = two_conns)$Global.Mean
  time <- aggregate("years"); event <- aggregate("event"); age <- aggregate("age")
  n <- time[1, "Nvalid"]
  events <- round(event[1, "EstimatedMean"] * n)
  py <- time[1, "EstimatedMean"] * n
  data.frame(Arm = c("Diclofenac", "Celecoxib")[arm + 1], People = n,
    Events = events, Person_years = py, Rate_per_1000 = 1000 * events / py,
    Mean_followup_days = 365.25 * py / n, Mean_age = age[1, "EstimatedMean"])
}))
arm_summary
Arm People Events Person_years Rate_per_1000 Mean_followup_days Mean_age
Diclofenac 830 124 710.05 174.64 312.46 38.10
Celecoxib 1800 355 1470.74 241.37 298.44 38.17

Celecoxib contributes 1,800 people, 355 events and 1,470.74 person-years; diclofenac contributes 830 people, 124 events and 710.05 person-years. The crude rates are about 241 and 175 per 1,000 person-years. Read the age and follow-up columns too: unequal follow-up is why a comparison of raw event counts would mislead.

Fit an adjusted survival model with dsBase

An exponential survival model assumes a constant event hazard during follow-up. Fit a Poisson model of the event indicator with log(person-years) as an offset. The treatment coefficient is a log hazard ratio against diclofenac, conditional on completed age at entry. This is not a Cox model.

dsBaseClient::ds.log("D_comparison_model$years", newobj = "log_years", datasources = two_conns)
comparison_fit <- dsBaseClient::ds.glm("event ~ celecoxib + age",
  data = "D_comparison_model", family = "poisson", offset = "log_years", datasources = two_conns)
beta <- comparison_fit$coefficients["celecoxib", "Estimate"]
se <- comparison_fit$coefficients["celecoxib", "Std. Error"]
data.frame(Hazard_ratio = exp(beta),
  Lower_95 = exp(beta - 1.96 * se), Upper_95 = exp(beta + 1.96 * se))
Hazard_ratio Lower_95 Upper_95
1.38 1.124 1.692

After age adjustment, celecoxib starters have about 1.38 times the bleeding hazard of diclofenac starters (95% CI about 1.12–1.69), under the constant-hazard assumption. Age adjustment alone cannot remove confounding by indication, selection or outcome misclassification; this synthetic association is not a causal drug effect.

Exercises

1. Compare crude and adjusted results. Calculate the crude incidence-rate ratio from the arm table. Does agreement establish adequate adjustment?

Solution 1

data.frame(Crude_rate_ratio = arm_summary$Rate_per_1000[2] /
  arm_summary$Rate_per_1000[1], Adjusted_hazard_ratio = exp(beta))
Crude_rate_ratio Adjusted_hazard_ratio
1.382 1.38

Both ratios are about 1.38. Similar estimates only show that this age adjustment changes little here; they do not rule out other confounding.

2. Check censoring. How many episodes end before day 365 without bleeding?

Solution 2

ds.omop.mutate("D_comparison", early_censor = ifelse(event == 0 & follow_up_days < 364, 1L, 0L),
  newobj = "D_censor", conns = two_conns)
dsBaseClient::ds.table("D_censor$early_censor",
  datasources = two_conns)$output.list$TABLES.COMBINED_all.sources_counts
#> D_censor$early_censor
#>    0    1   NA
#> 2578   52    0

The 52 early censored episodes end at observation end; GiBleed has no recorded deaths. Event-free follow-up through day 365 has elapsed duration 364 from day 1. Censoring means the outcome is unknown after follow-up ends, not that it never occurs.

Recap

Find standard ingredients and their descendants, make new-user entry mutually exclusive, declare time at risk and censoring, then pool a model with an explicit survival assumption. Protected tables and model diagnostics remain part of interpretation.
